points.form: 本日はお忙しい中 / お忙しいところ + coming/attendance + thanks
points.formation: お忙しい + 中 (なか) / ところ; guests perform the arrival/attendance, which the host acknowledges as a received favour.
points.teachingChoice: A conventional gratitude opening suited to an invited-client exhibition. Do not equate this なか with the suffix 中 (ちゅう) in 懇談中.

points.form: Vていただき / ご出席いただき + thanks
points.formation: Vte + いただき connecting to thanks; suru-action ごNいただき in the appropriate frame.
points.teachingChoice: Actual earlier or current help/attendance is thanked. Contrast with the previously taught conditional request いただければ幸いです. Guests are the arriving actors; own-side introduction and a direct address to one’s manager are kept distinct.

points.formation: Na-adjectival noun stem + concessive ながら; no simultaneous-action interpretation here.
points.teachingChoice: Bunpro supplies state/na-stem attachment; Zexy’s author/supervisor explains a modest preface to an assigned public toast role, using the related ではございますが formula. This is corroboration of function, not a claim that Zexy gives the exact ながら variant. A fixed expression recognised at N1 is not an official N1-only rule.

points.form: 以上をもちまして + named part/event + ending; ご唱和 cue
points.formation: Formal boundary をもって, polite continuation もちまして; explicitly name the remarks or the whole exhibition. ご唱和をお願いします cues the shared word 乾杯.
points.teachingChoice: Retrieves unit 2’s formal boundary. In the original programme opening remarks end near ten, exhibition at eleven, gathering starts eleven-ten. The shared spoken toast is distinct from drinking, standing or draining a glass.

sourceCautions: MLC business_japanese closing example appears to omit を; that spelling is not adopted.

Zexy’s wedding-specific taboo words and etiquette are not universal rules for a daytime work exhibition. Its template sentences are not copied as lesson paragraphs.
